title: One cursor, several kinds of evidence
summary: Graph, Table, and Map use the same log-time context, so a moment can be inspected without translating three unrelated clocks in your head.

blocks.text: A Blackbox event does not always carry its own timestamp. Airframe preserves event order and, where necessary, uses the latest valid main-frame time as its context. That makes an event useful on the timeline, but it does not manufacture precision the log never recorded.

items: Graph is the quickest way to see relationships and timing across signals.
Table is the place for exact displayed samples and decoded event rows.
Map binds the same moment to the most recent retained GPS route point.

blocks.title: The cursor is precise; the source may not be
blocks.text: A gap, low logging rate, sparse GPS samples, or an event without a payload timestamp limits what can honestly be concluded. Zooming farther in does not negotiate with physics—or missing bytes.
